content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.27 or +0.23) — model tends to overshoot and then correct sharply.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (avg -0.11 or below) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns positive after negative streaks, leading to premature price hikes.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices in early days of forecast window — correct by reducing initial forecast values by 0.5–1.5 units if sentiment is negative.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high peaks too long; reduce forecast slope after 5–7 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- Overshoots after spikes are common — if model forecasts >75.00 after a spike, reduce by 2–4 units unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Sentiment history with multiple -0.11 values suggests model should not assume continuation of trend — apply downward bias of 0.3–0.7 units per 3-day window if sentiment remains negative.
